blocking_findings.description: Round two's blocker 3 was fixed in the payload but not in the durable decision that justifies it, so the D1 trace is now false in exactly the way the round-two D5 trace was. session-log.md:11 records the Implementation decision as `**Use portable canonical guide links** `architectural: skill-workflow` -- Installed skill payloads cannot use relative links that escape the skill directory; a stable repository URL remains clickable in canonical and mirrored copies.` No stable repository URL exists anywhere in the branch any more: all six sources now carry the bare backticked path (`grep -rn state-artifacts skills/**/SKILL.md` returns the identical sentence at skills/autopilot/SKILL.md:17, skills/autopilot-roadmap/SKILL.md:16, skills/session-log/SKILL.md:15, skills/supervise/SKILL.md:17, skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md:22, skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md:22), and the test constant was renamed accordingly from `GUIDE_LINK` to `GUIDE_REFERENCE = "docs/guides/state-artifacts.md"` (test_state_artifacts_guide.py:16). A repo-wide grep for `github.com/jankneumann/agentic-coding-tools/blob/main/docs/guides/state-artifacts` outside `reviews/` returns nothing. The decision's own title is also now inaccurate -- a bare backticked path is a reference, not a link, and nothing rendered is clickable. The consequence is worse than a stale sentence because docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md:12 carries the same text verbatim: that file is generated by `PhaseRecord.write_both()` step four, which skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:355-372 documents as running 'last, and unconditionally' precisely because 'a session-log entry is the only thing that invalidates that index'. So the capability timeline -- the artifact every future skill-workflow change inherits its conventions from -- now publishes a rationale for a URL convention this branch deliberately abandoned, and hand-editing the generated file would be overwritten on the next session-log write.
